transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-17
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees (Redwood): Samira Khan, Miguel Ortega, Priya Desai
Attendees (Aperture Health): Lena Park, Marcus Hill, Sofia Reyes, Devon Cole

Summary:
Short demo showing the Redwood model sourcing workflow (catalog + playground), how benchmarks are captured into the bench spreadsheet, and how the compatibility matrix and Optimize recommendations tie into a pilot. Aperture is evaluating open models for clinical summarization and triage; main constraints are latency under 300ms 95th, data residency (US-East), and SOC2/compliance.

Topics covered:
- Quick intro & goals
- Catalog browsing and filtering for clinical-safe models
- Playground: prompt set, batch bench capture, token accounting
- Compatibility matrix: hardware mapping, quantization notes, kernel caveats
- Optimize recommendations: batching, cache, quantization profile suggestions
- Pilot and pricing options (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- Security/compliance Q&A (SSO, KMS, audit logs)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira Khan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick intro — I'm Samira, AE on the inference team, with Miguel, our SE, and Priya from product. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Lena Park: Good, thanks. We, we are excited to see how you all handle clinical prompts.
[00:10] Marcus Hill: Hi. We're mostly focused on latency and being able to run the models in region, and also cost but, you know, quality first.
[00:17] Samira Khan: Totally, makes sense. Our plan today is a short walkthrough of the catalog and a live playground demo of sampling benchmarks, then show how that data surfaces into the compatibility matrix and Optimize recommendations. We'll leave time for security questions at the end.
[00:29] Miguel Ortega: Quick note, if we hit anything too technical I'll pause and explain — but we'll try to keep it concrete.
[00:34] Sofia Reyes: Cool. Also Marcus, FYI, we've got some prompts that include PHI, so Devon will probably ask about retention.
[00:40] Devon Cole: Yep, retention and key management are the big ones for us.
[00:43] Samira Khan: Understood. We'll flag the playground as a synthetic prompt run — but we'll cover how Private or Dedicated keeps data in your VPC and KMS/HSM integration.

[02:05] Miguel Ortega: (screen share) Alright, starting in the Redwood Console — here's the model catalog. We filter by "open models" and then by token cost and tail-latency. See these tags — clinical, ft-safe, quant-ready — those are curated.
[02:20] Marcus Hill: Can you show how the compatibility matrix works? We want to know if the 13B opt variant will run on our A100-ish fleet or if we need to convert.
[02:29] Miguel Ortega: Sure. Clicking into the model shows the compatibility tab — it maps runtimes, recommended kernels, and known issues. For example, this 13B model recommends FP16 kernels on A100 and a specific fused attention kernel for long-context. We also show quantization impact: 8-bit and 4-bit profiles with expected latency/cost deltas.
[02:50] Lena Park: Are those bench numbers from Redwood infra or community runs?
[02:54] Miguel Ortega: Mostly Redwood-run with a mixture of internal lab bench sprints and verified community contributions. Each entry links to a bench sheet row with the prompt set used, sequence length distribution, and hardware.

[05:08] Samira Khan: I want to emphasize the bench spreadsheet — it's the single source of truth for any pilot. We'll pre-populate it with your prompts and a few synthetic PHI-safe examples so we can estimate token counts and 95th percentile latencies.
[05:22] Sofia Reyes: When you say pre-populate, does that mean we upload our exact prompts? We can't upload real PHI to hosted.
[05:30] Priya Desai: Good question — you can do three things: run the sprint in a sandbox with de-identified copies, run it in your Dedicated pool where logs are isolated, or run the bench locally and upload stats only. We have an upload template that accepts aggregate metrics so no raw PHI needs to leave your control.
[05:47] Devon Cole: And key management? KMS?
[05:50] Miguel Ortega: For Dedicated and Private, you can bring your own KMS/HSM and we integrate via the control plane so keys never land in Redwood-managed plaintext. For hosted you'd use our managed KMS but we can discuss an enterprise key contract.

[07:14] Miguel Ortega: Ok demo: switching to the Playground, we drop in a short sample prompt set — a triage prompt, discharge summary condense, and a follow-up note generator. I set the sequence to 512 tokens to match your long notes. Hitting run will capture token breakdown and produce a bench row entry.
[07:35] (audio: typing, pause)
[07:46] Miguel Ortega: The run finishes. You can see token cost, latencies per token, and the 95th percentile estimate. There's also a flag that suggests whether prefix caching would've helped — see here, for the triage prompts there's a high overlap so KV cache would cut cost significantly.
[08:10] Marcus Hill: That caching note is huge. In our pipeline we often have repeated templates. How do we control cache size?
[08:16] Miguel Ortega: You set cache TTL and max-kv-size per route. Optimize will suggest values based on observed repetition in your prompts.

[10:02] Samira Khan: Now the compatibility matrix — here's where bench entries aggregate to give hardware recommendations. For your triage workload, 8-bit quant with a specific kernel mapping on NVIDIA T4 gives best $$ per token for batch sizes of 8, but for latency under 300ms you'd look at an A10 or A100 and a slightly different profile.
[10:22] Sofia Reyes: Do you automate kernel selection across clouds? We use multiple cloud regions.
[10:27] Miguel Ortega: Yes, the runtime picks kernels per node type. The matrix preserves per-region availability. You can pin a model version and Redwood will route to the best-compatible variant per policy (latency, cost, region).

[12:40] Marcus Hill: Question on failover — if a model variant isn't available, can Redwood fall back to a lighter model? We can't have triage failing during peak hours.
[12:47] Priya Desai: Yes, the routing policy supports fallback chains: primary model, then a compatible smaller variant, then a hosted cold path. You define SLOs and fallback thresholds.

[14:55] Devon Cole: Security question: audit logs and retention, how granular are they? We need per-request logs for 90 days and token-level cost accounting for billing audits.
[15:05] Miguel Ortega: We provide per-request metadata (timestamps, model version, route, cost estimate) in the audit logs and you can configure retention. For Private, logs are delivered to your SIEM or S3 in encrypted form.
[15:21] Devon Cole: Do logs contain PII?
[15:23] Samira Khan: We redact or exclude request bodies by default. For Dedicated/Private you control logging policy so you can avoid storing raw request text.

[17:02] Miguel Ortega: Back to Optimize — here's the recommendation panel. It will rate your config for cost/latency and give specific suggestions: increase batch window from 8ms to 15ms for throughput, enable prefix cache on routes with repeated prompts, or switch to 4-bit quant profile for non-critical summarization jobs. Each recommendation includes expected delta and risk score.
[17:26] Marcus Hill: How accurate are those deltas? We're sensitive to both underestimating latency and overestimating cost savings.
[17:32] Miguel Ortega: Deltas are derived from bench runs and augmented with a small uncertainty margin; we also surface confidence levels and the underlying bench rows so you can validate.

[20:10] Sofia Reyes: A small transcription hiccup: I see references to 'kv cache' as 'k v cache' sometimes in the docs, not sure if that's consistent, sorry — the auto-docs occasionally word-split acronyms.
[20:22] Priya Desai: Noted, it happens. We'll correct the export but the meaning is KV (key-value) cache.

[22:00] Samira Khan: Let's talk pilot options quickly. Hosted is fastest but not ideal for PHI. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and isolation without full private deployment. Private is full-on VPC/on-prem and includes your KMS. For a 3-month pilot: we typically recommend starting with Dedicated in US-East, run two bench sprints, and then evaluate a private rollout if retention or regulatory concerns persist.
[22:30] Marcus Hill: Cost ballpark? We're looking at 10–20 M tokens/day for triage plus bursts.
[22:36] Samira Khan: We'll send a tailored cost model. Roughly speaking, Dedicated reserved pools reduce per-token compute by 20–40% vs hosted at scale, but there's a commit. We'll include a few scenarios in the spreadsheet.

[25:12] Miguel Ortega: Demoing a bench aggregation now — selecting multiple bench rows yields a combined compatibility recommendation and an expected cost curve by QPS. See the shaded area? That's the expected 95th latency envelope.
[25:25] Lena Park: That viz is very helpful. Do you support custom metrics? For example, our triage has an accuracy threshold for false negatives.
[25:33] Miguel Ortega: Yes, you can add custom metric hooks. Our bench runner will capture model outputs and score them via your eval script (or ours) and record the metric on the bench row. We can extend the runner to call your private scoring endpoint if you want to keep data in-house.

[28:50] Sofia Reyes: There's a lot of talk about quantization; we need to be careful about A/B quality regressions. How do you support regressions?
[28:58] Priya Desai: We have quality monitoring dashboards tied to prompt sets and evals. If a quant profile causes a regression, Optimize can mark it as 'do not roll' and send an alert. Also the rollout tooling supports canary and A/B with automatic rollback on metric drift.

[31:40] Marcus Hill: On the integration side, what are the SDKs like? We use Python and Go.
[31:44] Miguel Ortega: We have first-class SDKs for Python, Go, and TypeScript plus a REST API. All of them support streaming, function/tool calling, and metadata headers for routing and billing.

[34:10] Devon Cole: Regarding compliance docs — can you share SOC2 and any pen test reports?
[34:15] Samira Khan: Yes, we'll send the security pack with SOC2 and a summary of recent pentests. For Dedicated/Private we include additional controls in the contract.

[36:00] Miguel Ortega: One more feature I want to show — "playground-to-pilot" button. It converts a bench row into a proposed pilot configuration: model version, runtime profile, cache/batching, and a roll-out policy. You can tweak and then export to a provisioning request.
[36:18] Marcus Hill: How long to provision a Dedicated pool?
[36:21] Priya Desai: Typical timeline is 2–4 weeks for initial Dedicated capacity depending on size and region; we can accelerate for pilots with cloud partner credits.

[39:05] Samira Khan: Ok let's open it for a quick round of clarifying questions.
[39:10] Lena Park: One: are the bench runs deterministic across different hardware revisions? We've seen A100 versions vary.
[39:16] Miguel Ortega: We tag bench rows with microcode and driver versions. The matrix surfaces known variance and we provide a delta bound.
[39:29] Sofia Reyes: Two: will Redwood take responsibility for producing the prompt-level cost estimates used in our billing dashboard?
[39:36] Samira Khan: Yes, the platform can emit tokenized breakdowns and cost at the route level for billing. For enterprise you can sync with your internal billing system.

[43:00] Devon Cole: Final point: we'd like explicit language in the SOW re: data handling for the pilot.
[43:05] Samira Khan: That's reasonable. We'll include a data handling addendum for the pilot.

[49:00] Samira Khan: Quick recap of next steps — Samira will send bench spreadsheet and cost scenarios; Miguel will prepare bench sprint plan; Marcus will send sample prompts and constraints; Devon will confirm compliance questions. We'll aim to schedule the bench sprint week of Jan 22.
[49:23] Marcus Hill: Sounds good.
[49:28] Lena Park: Thanks all.
[49:30] Samira Khan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links to the sheet and security pack.
